answer: Epoch-linked reputation vertex rule. Each identity’s interaction graph is reduced to a single vertex (a decayed sum of its counterparties), and a new epoch is admitted only if that vertex stays within a bounded distance of the prior epoch’s after normalizing for activity. A violet flag marks identities whose vertex jumps beyond tolerance, forcing re-verification. Enforcement is cheap per honest agent but costs an attacker one full epoch of real interactions per identity to establish a stable vertex, plus the basalt cost of repeated re-verification audits.
